text: One day Murlock returned from hunting. <break time="0.8s" /> And found his wife ill with a fever. <break time="0.8s" /> So confused in her mind. <break time="0.8s" /> That she did not even recognize him. <break time="0.8s" /> There was no doctor within miles. <break time="0.8s" /> And no neighbor to call. <break time="0.8s" /> And since she could not be left alone. <break time="0.8s" /> He had no choice. <break time="0.8s" /> But to care for her himself. <break time="0.8s" /> For three days. <break time="0.8s" /> He nursed her alone. <break time="0.8s" /> But on the third day. <break time="0.8s" /> She sank into unconsciousness. <break time="0.8s" /> And passed away. <break time="0.8s" /> Apparently without ever coming back. <break time="0.8s" /> To her senses. <break time="0.8s" /> From what we know. <break time="0.8s" /> Of a nature like his we may venture to fill in some of the details of the picture. <break time="0.8s" /> That my grandfather drew. <break time="0.8s" /> When he was convinced. <break time="0.8s" /> That she was dead. <break time="0.8s" /> Murlock had sense enough. <break time="0.8s" /> To remember. <break time="0.8s" /> That the dead must be prepared for burial. <break time="0.8s" /> In performing this sacred duty. <break time="0.8s" /> He made mistakes now and then. <break time="0.8s" /> Did certain things incorrectly. <break time="0.8s" /> And did others. <break time="0.8s" /> Which he had done correctly. <break time="0.8s" /> Over and over again. <break time="0.8s" /> He was surprised. <break time="0.8s" /> That he did not weep. <break time="0.8s" /> And he felt a little ashamed of it. <break time="0.8s" /> For surely it is unkind. <break time="0.8s" /> Not to weep over the dead. <break time="0.8s" /> Tomorrow, he said aloud. <break time="0.8s" /> I shall have to make the coffin. <break time="0.8s" /> And dig the grave. <break time="0.8s" /> But things cannot be so bad. <break time="0.8s" /> As they seem.
